opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst. She requested admin to Payroll, but admin is reserved for the Payroll Specialist role owner. As a full-time employee, max is write; recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E002 is a contractor with basic security training (note: differs from HR's full_time listing). Contractors max out at read without advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Requested: admin to Payroll. Per policy, admin is only allowed for full-time employees whose role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and Erika Bolton (E002) is an Analyst, so admin is not permitted. Per HR records she is a full-time employee, whose maximum is write. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), grant the maximum: write.
